findings.statement: Observed: A white page contains a thin dark bordered card with a bold Sign in heading.
Observed: The card has an Email address label and input showing the name@example.com placeholder.
Observed: The card has a Password label and input illustrated with masked asterisks; the image does not establish functional masking or the field's actual placeholder behavior.
Observed: A blue underlined Forgot password? link is visible on the card; its activation is not depicted.
Observed: A dark rectangular Sign in button is visible; submission and sign-in outcomes are not depicted.
Observed: Grey footer text reads No account? Contact your administrator.; no footer interaction is established.

Observed: The only visible card controls are the email input, password input, Forgot password? link, and Sign in button; no other card controls are shown. No other screen, interaction, focus, error, loading, responsive behavior, or exact design token is evidenced.

Proposed: Activating the pictured Forgot password? link starts a separate reset-request interaction without adding a visible control to the sign-in card; the static image establishes the link's presence, not navigation.

Proposed: A reset-request screen accepts an account identifier and returns the same neutral request response for an existing or nonexistent account, with no account-existence clue in its response content; a neutral acknowledgment is not confirmation that a link exists.

Proposed: Enforce five reset requests per synthetic account per hour behind the UI; another request within that hour must not create another usable link, while its returned request response stays consistent with the identical-response rule. This limit is not an observed control or a specified nonexistent-account accounting rule.

Proposed: A valid-link reset-completion interaction accepts a new password for the corresponding synthetic account only while an unused link is valid. A link works before issuance plus 30 minutes, cannot reset at or after that boundary, and cannot complete a second reset after successful use; present invalid, expired, or used-link recovery guidance without claiming a depicted form or password policy.

Proposed: Following every successful reset, invalidate all active sessions for that account and record an owner notification for that success. A completion result can guide return to sign-in; it must not imply an old session remains authenticated or that notification is delivered through a production service. These are application effects, not observed UI.

Proposed: Limit the demonstration to synthetic accounts, with reset links and owner notifications test-inspectable in memory; do not represent a link or owner notification as externally delivered. These boundaries have no direct visual evidence.

Proposed: Document production limitations, including synthetic accounts and in-memory notifications, and provide automated tests for the observed sign-in inventory and specified reset behaviors. Documentation and test completion are nonvisual obligations, not shown or verified by the wireframe.
Proposed: Do not deploy the application or add deployment workflows; these delivery constraints have no on-screen representation or visual evidence.

Proposed: On the sign-in screen, distinguish empty fields, locally invalid identifiers and invalid synthetic credentials using labeled textual feedback; announce pending submission and a minimal local success/result without adding permanent visible controls to the pictured card. The exact sign-in outcome, validation rules, and copy remain undecided.

Proposed: On the reset-request screen, identify empty or locally invalid input accessibly without testing account existence in field errors; communicate pending submission and generic service failure. The ordinary completed-request acknowledgment, including a rate-limited request, must preserve the same response for existing and nonexistent accounts.

Proposed: Treat the neutral acknowledgment as a distinct no-input result state: its returned content must not confirm account existence, link generation, or delivery; any loading or generic error must not reveal account-specific status.

Proposed: On reset completion/result, prompt for an empty new password, show pending submission without duplicate completion, and provide accessible recovery guidance for invalid, expired, or used links. Only a valid unused link before issuance plus 30 minutes can lead to a successful password-change result; exact form fields, policy, and wording remain open.

Proposed: Across sign-in and proposed recovery screens, enable logical keyboard order and activation, visible focus, programmatic labels and discernible link/button names, field-linked textual errors, and screen-reader announcements for progress and results without account disclosure. Check contrast for the depicted blue link, grey footer and dark button as well as proposed errors and focus states; no conformance or color tokens can be inferred from the image.

assumptions: Observed details are limited to the supplied sign-in wireframe. No interactivity, other screen, responsive layout, error or focus state, or design token is inferred from the static image.
The approved requirements were read for their identifiers and text, but the stage-output reader supplied no source-reference locator; no stage_output citation is fabricated.
Only minimal local synthetic-account sign-in/session behavior is contemplated to exercise sign-in and all-session invalidation; no production session infrastructure is assumed.

The specified five-per-account-per-hour limit applies to synthetic accounts while returned request responses remain identical for existing and nonexistent accounts; counting and throttling nonexistent identifiers is unresolved.
Links and owner notifications are inspectable through a local in-memory mechanism; no external link transport or production email/SMS delivery is assumed.

A minimal reset-completion interaction changes the synthetic account password; no password complexity policy, confirmation field, pixel-exact layout, or additional permanent sign-in-card control is assumed.

open_questions.question: What layout and exact neutral acknowledgment copy should the proposed recovery screens use, and should the identifier be re-entered or carried forward?
open_questions.context: The wireframe shows only sign-in. Any carried identifier must not vary the existing/nonexistent request response.

open_questions.question: How will local synthetic-account reset links be surfaced and the in-memory notification sink inspected?
open_questions.context: Do not imply an external delivery channel or disclose account existence in the request response.

open_questions.question: How should nonexistent identifiers be counted or throttled without disclosing account existence?
open_questions.context: The standard specifies five requests per account per hour but does not define a nonexistent-account key or threshold.

open_questions.question: What are the new-password fields, password policy, and expired/used-link recovery wording?
open_questions.context: No recovery form or password complexity rule is provided by the wireframe or standard.

open_questions.question: What is the sign-in success destination and how will multiple local sessions be represented and verified?
open_questions.context: Only a minimal synthetic-account session behavior is assumed; the sign-in button's behavior is not pictured.

open_questions.question: What responsive layout, contrast tokens, focus placement, and screen-reader announcements should be adopted?
open_questions.context: The static wireframe supplies neither responsive states nor measurable accessibility behavior.
